text:
Copilot connectors: stop pasting your database schema.
GitHub added Supabase and seven more service connectors in public preview on Nov. 18. Copilot can inspect connected project context before suggesting a change.
On Tech Thursday, we used MCP from Copilot CLI to request an image batch. Different task, same bridge: connect the tool, then inspect the result.
Try a read-only schema summary on a test Supabase project this week. Keep writes off. The useful shift is from explaining your workspace to working inside its context.
Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

text:
Copilot Evals: a finished batch can still fail the brief.
GitHub's Nov. 17 public preview adds repeatable checks for skills, agents and MCP tools. You can compare behavior before and after a customization change.
On Tech Thursday, our MCP image batch ran, but the host said the images missed the quality he wanted. Execution wasn't acceptance.
Try one eval this week: the same brief, explicit brand criteria, then a rerun after one prompt change. Keep human visual review. Creators need evidence a workflow improved, not just another completed run.
Follow @layer8culture if you're building with AI.

text:
AI coding: make failure visible before you automate.
A missing output file should stop the job, not produce a success message.
For your next script: check the required file, report what's missing, exit with an error. Quiet failures become expensive habits.
Follow @layer8culture for practical AI building habits.

text:
GitHub Copilot browser use: let it click the page, then check the result.

GitHub's Nov. 17 public preview brings browser use to Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, VS Code and JetBrains through its Chrome extension.

It can interact with a web app while you debug or test. For a creator building a landing page, that means checking the visitor's path, not only the code behind it.

Our latest Tech Thursday recap included building a website together and helping a newcomer into the terminal. Browser use is a next experiment for that kind of build, not something we're claiming we tested on the show.

Try this week:
1. Install the GitHub Copilot Chrome extension and enable browser use in your client. In CLI, enable it through /plugin and start a new session.
2. Use a disposable local page with a form. No real customer data or accounts.
3. Ask it to submit an empty form and report the visible validation response. Compare the report with what you see.

A click is an action. A checked result is workflow evidence. Keep permissions narrow and production publishing under human approval.

Save this for your next landing-page build.

Copilot Evals asks the question a completed image batch can't answer: did it meet the brief?

GitHub put repeatable checks for skills, agents and MCP tools into public preview on Nov. 17. Builders can compare runs after changing a customization.

The latest Tech Thursday gave us the reason to care: we used MCP through Copilot CLI to request images, then the host reviewed the batch and said it wasn't the quality he wanted. The tool ran. The creative bar was still ours to hold.

One experiment for this week: turn a recurring creative brief into explicit checks, rerun it after one prompt change, and compare the results. Keep a human on visual judgment; an automated check isn't your creative director.

That's the move from a completed task to a workflow you can evaluate.

Follow @layer8culture for AI builds with a visible quality bar.

Copilot + Supabase: start with a schema read, not a database write.

On Nov. 18, GitHub added eight service connectors in public preview, including Supabase, Box and Calendly. Copilot can use connected service context instead of asking you to paste it all into a chat.

For developers and creator-operators, the useful part is a smaller handoff between the workspace and the build partner.

On our latest Tech Thursday, MCP let Copilot CLI request an image batch. These new connectors serve different tools, but the builder lesson carries: a connection needs a defined task and a checked result.

Try this week: connect a disposable Supabase project with read-only access and ask for a schema summary. Compare it with the actual tables. Don't grant writes for a reading task. Organization policies may control preview access.

AI fluency includes knowing what the tool can reach, not only what to ask it.
